about.title: Downey Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Downey is served by major hospitals and clinics across southeast Los Angeles County, and while most care is competent, preventable errors do happen — misdiagnoses, delayed treatment, surgical mistakes, medication errors and birth injuries. California medical malpractice law is technical and time-sensitive: it carries its own filing deadlines, procedural notice requirements, and — unlike ordinary injury cases — a statutory cap on non-economic damages that increases over time. Because of that complexity, having the right attorney early matters. LawProactive connects patients and families, at no cost, with an independent medical malpractice attorney. You pay no fee unless the case recovers compensation.

items.title: Special California deadlines
items.desc: Medical malpractice claims follow their own statute of limitations — generally one year from discovery, up to three years from the injury — with a notice requirement before filing. Missing these can end an otherwise strong case.

items.title: Expert proof is required
items.desc: These cases almost always need a qualified medical expert to establish that care fell below the accepted standard. Attorneys in our network work with the right experts.

items.title: A cap you should understand
items.desc: California limits non-economic damages in malpractice cases under a schedule that rises each year. An attorney can explain how it applies to your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally one year from when you discovered (or should have discovered) the injury, and no more than three years from the date it occurred, with exceptions. California also requires giving the provider 90 days' notice before filing, so speak with an attorney promptly.

items.question: A bad outcome happened — is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Medicine carries risk, and a poor result alone isn't enough. Malpractice means the care fell below the accepted professional standard and that failure caused harm — something a medical expert must typically confirm.

items.question: What will a case review cost me?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. The review is free and malpractice attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no attorney fee unless they recover compensation for you.
